items.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021
items.q: Then Leon was doing yodeling. And then I was doing a little bit different things on the keyboard so Pharoah said man, you know why don’t we all just get together? And it worked.

ctx.x: Did Leon Thomas have that kind of flexibility?

Yeah, oh yeah. That was the thing about Leon, that’s how we all got together. Because I said well dang, how can you play more than one note? You know with a horn player, can’t play but one note at a time. But he has figured out ways to sound like he’s playing more than one note. Then Leon was doing yodeling. And then I was doing a little bit different things on the keyboard so Pharoah said man, you know why don’t we all just get together? And it worked. Because no one else was doing the yodeling at that time like…

I wonder if that has anything to do with technology. If we look back on the 70s we sort of smile at the level of technology was so far behind where it is now, but as you say, there was some great creativity going on at that time.
